title: Object Lifecycle, Duplication, and Freezing
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of object lifecycle, duplication, and freezing in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply object lifecycle, duplication, and freezing in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to freezing objects for safer use and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Object Lifecycle, Duplication, and Freezing through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding object lifecycle, duplication, and freezing helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Object Lifecycle, Duplication, and Freezing helps you reason about object creation and allocation. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Object creation and allocation. Then connect it to Copies of mutable state. The remaining syllabus points—Freezing objects for safer use—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Object Lifecycle, Duplication, and Freezing
content_blocks.code:
class Greeter
  def initialize(name)
    @name = name
  end
  def greet
    "Hello, #{@name}!"
  end
end
puts Greeter.new("Mina").greet

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports object lifecycle, duplication, and freezing. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.text: Create a second example for object lifecycle, duplication, and freezing using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Freezing objects for safer use), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain object lifecycle, duplication, and freezing, identify its place in object-oriented programming, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
